counterhypotheses: Simple key rotation with an independently pinned public-key registry and retired prior keys may yield the same historical-forgery behavior; external witness assumptions may be unavailable or a signed false claim may remain undetected.

decision_gates.comparison_interpretation: Even if the finite method gate passes, record NO_DISTINCT_HISTORICAL_FORGERY_ADVANTAGE_OVER_ROTATING_KEYS_ON_THIS_FIXTURE. No scheme-level FSS security conclusion is made.
decision_gates.fail: Any candidate/auditor disagreement, invalid positive history, accepted registered historical forgery, mutation confusion, missingness-as-zero, or claim that signature validity proves effect truth.
decision_gates.method_pass: All frozen positive and negative behaviors match the independent audit, including equal tested historical-forgery rejection for rotating and evolving keys; only checkpointed validation rejects current-head rewrite/fork and latest-prefix rollback; the false claim remains authenticated but scorer-false.

hypothesis: Under the fixture's hash-based one-time-key assumptions, the disclosed period-4 compromise leaf cannot authenticate a period-1 record; the separately registered rotating-key baseline may provide the same tested historical-forgery rejection. Without an external current-head witness, a valid current key can produce a conflicting suffix or a verifier can accept a shorter valid prefix; the checkpointed variant should reject those alternatives. Authentic signatures do not establish the truth of signed claims.

runtime.memory_enforcement: UNVERIFIED; WSLc stderr warns swap-limit capabilities are unsupported or cgroup is not mounted.

test: Freeze four synthetic periods, two one-time slots per period, public-key/root/checkpoint bytes, and input records. Compare independently registered period keys; a Merkle/Lamport frontier whose consumed leaves are discarded; and that frontier plus an independent one-time checkpoint witness. Candidate and raw-only auditor each run once, no retries. Mutation cases: current-leaf historical forgery, body alteration, interior deletion, current suffix rewrite, fork, valid-prefix rollback, wrong-period signature, invalid signature, missing/stale checkpoint, state rollback/skip, and correctly signed false-effect claim.
uncertainty: Finite four-period SHA-256/Lamport construction only. It is not a standardized production FSS implementation or a cryptographic proof. Process-level pruning is not evidence of physical secure erasure. No monotonic-time, witness-honesty, task-effect truth, runtime, GUI, model, input, safety or deployment conclusion.
